gloss: To force something into a space or a schedule that is really too small for it.
examples: Try not to *shoehorn* three topics into one slide.
They *shoehorned* a second bedroom into the attic.
The director is *shoehorning* a love story into the plot.

gloss: To make a person or an animal go away by waving at them.
examples: Don't *shoo* the birds off the feeder.
The waiter *shooed* the cat out of the kitchen.
She stood in the doorway, *shooing* the kids back inside.
contrast: The past is *shooed*. *Shoed* belongs to *shoe* — putting shoes on a horse.

gloss: To give someone less than they are owed, in money or in fair treatment.
examples: Count your change so the cashier can't *shortchange* you.
The clerk *shortchanged* him by five dollars.
Rural schools have been *shortchanged* for decades.

ru: включать в шорт-лист, включить в окончательный список
gloss: To put someone or something on the short list of final candidates.
examples: The committee will *shortlist* five architects next week.
Her novel was *shortlisted* for the national prize.
They are *shortlisting* applicants all this month.

ru: рисоваться, покрасоваться; выпендриваться, работать на публику
gloss: To show off in a flashy way in order to get attention.
examples: Good players pass the ball; they don't *showboat*.
He *showboated* after the touchdown and drew a penalty.
The crowd hates it when a driver starts *showboating*.

transitivity: both — transitive (*she shrieked his name*), intransitive (*the baby shrieked*)
gloss: To give a loud, high, sharp cry.
examples: The kids *shriek* every time the roller coaster drops.
She *shrieked* when the lights went out.
We could hear the brakes *shrieking* around the corner.

gloss: To strip the husk or shell off corn, peas, or oysters.
examples: We *shuck* the corn outside so the husks stay off the floor.
He *shucked* two dozen oysters in ten minutes.
She sat on the porch *shucking* peas into a bowl.

ru: отодвигать, отодвинуть в сторону; спихивать, спихнуть
gloss: To move someone or something aside, usually to a less important place.
examples: Don't *shunt* the problem to another department.
The complaint was *shunted* from office to office.
Management keeps *shunting* him into jobs nobody wants.

gloss: To tell someone to be quiet.
examples: Please don't *shush* me in front of the class.
The librarian *shushed* the whole table.
He kept *shushing* the dog while he was on the call.

ru: вызывать отвращение, вызвать отвращение; внушать омерзение
gloss: To make someone feel disgust or physical revulsion.
examples: Stories like that *sicken* me.
The smell of the sewer *sickened* everyone on the bus.
He was *sickened* by what he saw in the video.

transitivity: both — transitive (*sidestep the question*), intransitive (*he sidestepped quickly*)
gloss: To avoid something by moving around it instead of dealing with it.
examples: Politicians *sidestep* questions they can't answer.
She *sidestepped* the puddle without breaking stride.
He has been *sidestepping* the issue all week.

ru: задевать боком, задеть бортом; ударять вскользь, ударить вскользь
gloss: To hit something along its side while going past it.
examples: One wrong turn and you *sideswipe* the parked cars.
A truck *sideswiped* her car on the interstate.
The bus was *sideswiped* and lost a mirror.

ru: отвлекать, отвлечь; сбивать с темы, сбить с темы
gloss: To pull someone or something away from the main subject or task.
examples: Let's not *sidetrack* the meeting with budget talk.
I *sidetracked* myself reading email all morning.
We got *sidetracked* and never finished the report.

ru: подходить бочком, подойти бочком; двигаться боком
gloss: To move sideways, quietly and a little nervously.
examples: Salesmen always *sidle* over when you look lost.
A stranger *sidled* up to the bar beside him.
She was *sidling* toward the exit before the speech ended.

gloss: To be a sign of something, or to make something known.
examples: In court, silence does not *signify* guilt.
A raised hand *signified* that she wanted the floor.
Nothing in his tone had *signified* anger.

ru: обрисовывать силуэтом, обрисовать силуэтом; вырисовывать на фоне
gloss: To show something as a dark outline against a lighter background.
examples: Backlighting will *silhouette* the dancer against the screen.
The sunset *silhouetted* two riders on the ridge.
We saw the tower *silhouetted* against a gray sky.
contrast: The *h* is silent and the ending is French: *sil-oo-ET*.

gloss: To break a religious or moral law.
examples: He believes we all *sin* in small ways every day.
She confessed that she had *sinned*.
The sermon was about knowingly *sinning* and asking forgiveness.

gloss: To draw liquid off through a tube, or to take money away a little at a time.
examples: Thieves *siphon* gas out of parked trucks.
An official *siphoned* millions from the relief fund.
Money had been quietly *siphoned* into offshore accounts.
contrast: American spelling *siphon*; British writing also uses *syphon*.

gloss: To place something in a particular spot or in a particular context.
examples: The architects will *situate* the clinic near the highway.
She *situated* her novel in postwar Chicago.
The house is *situated* on a hill above the lake.

gloss: To leave somewhere quickly, often to avoid trouble.
examples: We'd better *skedaddle* before the rain starts.
The kids *skedaddled* the moment the door opened.
They were *skedaddling* down the alley when the siren started.

ru: искажать, исказить; смещать, сместить (в одну сторону)
transitivity: both — transitive (*that skews the results*), intransitive (*the audience skews older*)
gloss: To pull a result or a picture of something out of true in one direction.
examples: A few huge salaries *skew* the average.
Bad weather *skewed* the turnout figures.
The sample is *skewed* toward younger voters.

ru: насаживать на шампур, насадить; разносить в пух и прах, раскритиковать
gloss: To push a pointed stick through food, or to attack someone sharply in words.
examples: *Skewer* the shrimp and put them on the grill.
The columnist *skewered* the mayor's new plan.
Chicken and peppers were *skewered* together.

ru: сдирать кожу, содрать кожу; обдирать, ободрать (колено)
gloss: To take the skin off something, or to scrape the skin off part of your body.
examples: Hunters *skin* the animal right away.
He fell off his bike and *skinned* his knee.
The rabbit had already been *skinned* and cleaned.

gloss: To go around the edge of something, or to avoid dealing with it directly.
examples: The trail *skirts* the lake for about a mile.
His answer *skirted* the real question.
We drove all evening, *skirting* the worst of the storm.

gloss: To move or wait somewhere secretly, with bad intentions.
examples: Foxes *skulk* along the fence line after dark.
A man *skulked* near the loading dock for an hour.
Reporters were *skulking* outside the courthouse.

ru: прыгать с парашютом, прыгнуть с парашютом; заниматься парашютным спортом
gloss: To jump from an aircraft and fall freely before opening a parachute.
examples: You can *skydive* with an instructor on your first jump.
She *skydived* on her seventieth birthday.
They have been *skydiving* together for years.
contrast: The past is regular — *skydived*. *Skydove* is heard, but it is not the standard form.

ru: резко взлетать, взлететь (о ценах); стремительно расти, вырасти
gloss: To rise extremely fast.
examples: Rents *skyrocket* whenever a new campus opens.
Egg prices *skyrocketed* over the winter.
Demand has been *skyrocketing* since the video went viral.

ru: ослаблять, ослабить; замедляться, замедлиться; слабеть, ослабеть
transitivity: both — transitive (*slacken the rope*), intransitive (*the pace slackened*)
gloss: To become slower or looser, or to make something slower or looser.
examples: *Slacken* the rope a little before you tie it off.
The rain *slackened* around noon.
Demand has *slackened* since the holidays.

ru: наклонять, наклонить; иметь наклон; подавать тенденциозно, исказить подачу
transitivity: both — transitive (*slant the coverage*), intransitive (*the roof slants sharply*)
gloss: To lean at an angle, or to present information in a biased way.
examples: The old floorboards *slant* toward the back wall.
The network *slanted* its coverage of the strike.
He accused the paper of *slanting* every headline.

gloss: To spread something on thickly.
examples: *Slather* sunscreen on before you go out.
He *slathered* mustard across the whole sandwich.
The walls had been *slathered* with cheap paint.

gloss: To walk around while asleep.
examples: Some children *sleepwalk* for a few years and then stop.
He *sleepwalked* into the kitchen and opened the fridge.
She has been *sleepwalking* since the move.

gloss: To insult someone by treating them as unimportant.
examples: He didn't mean to *slight* anyone with the seating chart.
Leaving her off the program *slighted* the whole department.
She felt *slighted* and stopped coming to the meetings.

gloss: To let saliva run out of the mouth.
examples: Big dogs *slobber* all over the furniture.
The bulldog *slobbered* on my jeans.
He was *slobbering* into his pillow, sound asleep.

gloss: To keep working or walking through something slow and exhausting.
examples: Most nights I just *slog* through email.
We *slogged* up the hill in the rain.
She has been *slogging* away at the thesis for two years.

ru: иметь наклон; спускаться, опускаться; наклонять, наклонить
transitivity: both — transitive (*slope the deck for drainage*), intransitive (*the lawn slopes down*)
gloss: To lie or run at an angle rather than flat or straight.
examples: The yard *slopes* down toward the creek.
The old roof *sloped* so steeply we couldn't stand on it.
A long, gently *sloping* driveway leads to the house.

transitivity: both — transitive (*he sloshed water on the floor*), intransitive (*the coffee sloshed*)
gloss: To move noisily around inside a container, or to splash liquid about.
examples: Half-full bottles *slosh* the whole way home.
Coffee *sloshed* over the rim of the cup.
He walked slowly, the bucket *sloshing* against his leg.

ru: вставлять, вставить; помещать, поместить (в график, расписание)
gloss: To fit something into a particular place or time.
examples: We can *slot* you in at four o'clock.
The producer *slotted* the interview after the ads.
New hires are being *slotted* into existing teams.

gloss: To stand, sit, or walk with the shoulders drooping forward.
examples: Try not to *slouch* while you're on camera.
He *slouched* in the back row the whole hour.
She was *slouching* over her laptop again.

transitivity: both — transitive (*a snake sloughs its skin*), intransitive (*the dead skin sloughs away*)
gloss: To shed a layer of skin or dead tissue.
examples: Snakes *slough* their skin several times a year.
The burn *sloughed* a layer of dead tissue.
Old cells are constantly being *sloughed* off.
contrast: In this sense it is said SLUF, rhyming with *stuff* — not like *plough* or *through*.

ru: сильно бить кулаком, ударить кулаком; вмазать
gloss: To hit someone hard with your fist.
examples: Don't *slug* your brother over a video game.
He *slugged* the man who insulted his wife.
Two fans were *slugging* it out in the parking lot.

ru: резко падать, упасть (о ценах, спросе); опускаться, ссутулиться
gloss: To fall sharply in value, or to drop heavily into a sitting position.
examples: Sales always *slump* in January.
He *slumped* into the chair without a word.
Attendance has been *slumping* for three seasons.

transitivity: both — transitive (*he slurred his words*), intransitive (*she was slurring badly*)
gloss: To run words together so that they are hard to understand.
examples: Painkillers can make you *slur* your words.
He *slurred* the last half of the sentence.
She was *slurring* badly by the end of the night.

gloss: To turn the corners of your mouth up to show that you are pleased or friendly.
examples: Try to *smile* for the photo.
She *smiled* when she saw the address on the envelope.
He was *smiling* the whole way home.
contrast: You *smile at* someone: *she smiled at me*, never *she smiled me*.

gloss: To smile in a smug or knowing way that annoys other people.
examples: Don't *smirk* when someone else gets it wrong.
He *smirked* at the question and said nothing.
She kept *smirking* through the entire apology.

transitivity: both — transitive (*snake the drain*), intransitive (*the river snakes north*)
gloss: To follow a long, winding path, or to push a flexible tool through a pipe.
examples: The road *snakes* through the canyon for twenty miles.
A line of cars *snaked* around the block.
The plumber is *snaking* the kitchen drain right now.

ru: ловить в силки, поймать; заманивать в ловушку, заманить
gloss: To catch an animal in a trap, or to catch a person out.
examples: Poachers *snare* rabbits along the fence line.
The sting operation *snared* three officials.
He was *snared* by his own emails.

transitivity: both — transitive (*he snarled a warning*), intransitive (*the dog snarled*)
gloss: To growl with the teeth showing, or to speak in an angry, hostile way.
examples: Stray dogs *snarl* when you get too close.
He *snarled* an answer and hung up.
The guard stood there, *snarling* at anyone who came near.

gloss: To laugh quietly and unkindly.
examples: Students *snicker* whenever he mispronounces a name.
Someone *snickered* in the back of the room.
They were still *snickering* about it at lunch.
contrast: American English uses *snicker*; British writing uses *snigger*.

gloss: To breathe in noisily through a blocked or running nose.
examples: The kids *sniffle* all through allergy season.
She *sniffled* her way through the whole movie.
He sat *sniffling* into a paper towel.

transitivity: both — transitive (*snip the thread*), intransitive (*she snipped at the loose ends*)
gloss: To cut something with quick, small strokes of scissors.
examples: *Snip* the tag off before you wear it.
The nurse *snipped* the bandage in two.
He stood there *snipping* at the hedge.

gloss: To force air noisily out through the nose, often in scorn or laughter.
examples: Horses *snort* when they are nervous.
He *snorted* at the suggestion and walked off.
She was *snorting* with laughter by the second verse.

ru: расти как снежный ком, нарастать, нарасти; разрастаться, разрастись
gloss: To grow bigger and faster in a way that is hard to stop.
examples: Small repairs *snowball* into a full renovation.
The complaint *snowballed* into a federal investigation.
Costs have been *snowballing* since the delay.

gloss: To treat a room so that sound cannot get in or out.
examples: We need to *soundproof* the practice room.
They *soundproofed* the basement before the baby came.
The studio has been fully *soundproofed*.

transitivity: both — transitive (*the scandal soured relations*), intransitive (*the milk soured*)
gloss: To go bad, or to turn a relationship or a mood unpleasant.
examples: Milk will *sour* in a day at that temperature.
The deal *soured* after the audit.
Months of delays have been *souring* public opinion.

ru: закупать, закупить; находить поставщика; добывать, добыть
gloss: To find and obtain materials, parts, or staff from a supplier.
examples: We *source* the beans directly from growers.
They *sourced* the steel from three different mills.
All the wood is *sourced* locally.

ru: располагать с промежутками, расположить; распределять, распределить (по времени)
gloss: To arrange things with gaps between them, in a line or over time.
examples: *Space* the seedlings about a foot apart.
The doctor *spaced* the injections three weeks apart.
The fence posts are evenly *spaced*.

gloss: To stretch across something, in distance or in time.
examples: Two bridges *span* the river downtown.
Her career *spanned* four decades.
The study, *spanning* twelve countries, took six years.

gloss: To hit a child on the bottom with an open hand as punishment.
examples: Most schools no longer *spank* students.
His father *spanked* him for lying.
She grew up without ever being *spanked*.

gloss: To remove the ovaries of a female animal so that it cannot breed.
examples: The shelter will *spay* every cat before adoption.
We *spayed* her at six months.
All our dogs are *spayed* or neutered.
contrast: *Spay* is for females; a male animal is *neutered*.

gloss: To join two pieces end to end so that they work as one.
examples: You can *splice* the two cables with a connector.
The editor *spliced* the two takes together.
A gene had been *spliced* into the plant's DNA.

gloss: To imitate something in a joking way, or to fake an identity electronically.
examples: Late-night shows *spoof* the debates every four years.
Scammers *spoofed* the bank's phone number.
The ad is *spoofing* a famous movie trailer.

transitivity: both — transitive (*the noise spooked the herd*), intransitive (*the horse spooked and bolted*)
gloss: To frighten a person or an animal suddenly.
examples: Loud noises *spook* the horses.
The news *spooked* investors.
Something must have *spooked* her, because she left early.

ru: черпать ложкой, зачерпнуть; накладывать ложкой, наложить
gloss: To move food from one place to another with a spoon.
examples: *Spoon* the sauce over the fish before serving.
He *spooned* soup into a thermos.
She was *spooning* yogurt straight from the container.
